record.paper_title: Three Open Problems on the Wijsman Topology
record.original_question: Let (X, d) be a metric space. Let 2^X be the family of all non-empty closed subsets of X, and let T_W(d) be the Wijsman topology on 2^X; the Wijsman hyperspace of (X, d) is (2^X, T_W(d)). A space is pseudocomplete when it is quasi-regular and has a sequence of open pi-bases such that every nested sequence V_n, with closure(V_{n+1}) contained in V_n from the n-th pi-base, has non-empty intersection. Base-compactness and subcompactness are Amsterdam-style completeness properties defined using open bases and non-empty intersections for centered families or regular filterbases. If (X, d) is pseudocomplete, subcompact, or base-compact, must its Wijsman hyperspace have the corresponding property?

evidence.quote: Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space, and $2^X$ be the collection of all non-empty closed subsets of $X$.

The weakest topology on $2^X$ such that all functionals $d(\cdot, A)$, $A \in 2^X$, are continuous is called the \emph{Wijsman topology} and denoted by $\mathscr T_{W(d)}$. Correspondingly, we call $\left(2^X, \mathscr T_{W(d)}\right)$ the \emph{Wijsamn hyperspace} of $(X,d)$.

Recall that a topological space $X$ is said to be (resp. \emph{countably}) \emph{base compact} with respect to an open base $\mathfrak B$ if $X$ is regular such that $\bigcap_{F \in \mathscr F} \overline{F} \ne \varnothing$ for each (resp. countable) centered family ${\mathscr F} \subseteq \mathfrak B$, and $X$ is said to be (resp. \emph{countably}) \emph{subcompact} with respect to an open base $\mathfrak B$ if $X$ is regular such that $\bigcap_{F\in\mathscr F} \overline{F}\ne\varnothing$ for each (resp. countable) regular filterbase ${\mathscr F}\subseteq\mathfrak B$.

Recall that a topological space $X$ is said to be \emph{pseudocomplete} \cite{aarts:74} if $X$ is quasi-regular and has a sequence $\{\mathfrak P_n : n \in \mathbb N\}$ of open $\pi$-bases such that $\bigcap_{n\in \mathbb N} V_n \ne \varnothing$, whenever $\overline{V_{n+1}} \subseteq V_n \in \mathfrak P_n$ for each $n\in \mathbb N$.
Question 3.11 ([7]). If (X, d) is pseudocomplete (resp. subcompact, base-compact), must (2^X, T_W(d)) be pseudocomplete (resp. subcompact, base-compact)?

artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as one of three open problems on the Wijsman topology. Related work by Cao and Junnila on Amsterdam properties of Wijsman hyperspaces establishes partial results (e.g., existence of certain metric spaces whose Wijsman hyperspaces are almost countably subcompact or countably base-compact), but no resolution of the full preservation question for pseudocompleteness, subcompactness, or base-compactness has been located.

status_evidence.title: Three open problems on the Wijsman topology
status_evidence.snippet: Three open problems concerning the Wijsman hyperspace are formulated, including preservation of Amsterdam-style completeness properties.

status_evidence.title: Amsterdam properties of Wijsman hyperspaces (Cao-Junnila)
status_evidence.snippet: Partial results on subcompactness and base-compactness of Wijsman hyperspaces are obtained, but full preservation problem is left open.
